exposure: abscess and hematoma formation at the precedent cesarean section
minimal residual myometrial thickness (RMT) of ≦3.0 mm
RMT before and three-months after repair
abdominal repair surgery for cesarean scar defect (CSD)
cohort: 20 women who underwent abdominal repair for cesarean scar defect (CSD) with a minimal residual myometrial thickness (RMT) of ≦3.0 mm
finding: Abdominal repair for CSD in women with thin RMT who experience secondary infertility resulted in live births in seven women, with no surgical complications during repair and no uterine ruptures in subsequent pregnancies, except for one case of twin pregnancy requiring cesarean section due to bulging at the repair site.
mod_finding: Twin pregnancies following abdominal repair for CSD can promote thinning of the CSD repair site, potentially increasing the risk of uterine rupture.
